title: Optimal polynomial-time approximation ratio for Euclidean k-means
area: Approximation algorithms and hardness of approximation
formal: Determine \(\rho_{\mathrm{EucKM}}\), the infimum of achievable expected approximation ratios for Euclidean k-means with an unrestricted number of clusters and unrestricted dimension.
definitions: An instance consists of integers \(n,d\ge1\), \(1\le k\le n\), and a list of rational points \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb Q^d\), allowing repetitions. A solution is a list of exactly k centers \(c_1,\ldots,c_k\in\mathbb Q^d\), allowing repeated centers, of cost \(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\min_{j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}}\|x_i-c_j\|_2^2\). OPT is the minimum over k centers in \(\mathbb R^d\); an optimum has rational centers because each nonempty cluster can use its mean. Neither k nor d is fixed. Centers may be anywhere in the space and are not required to be input points. An algorithm is a uniform randomized Turing machine with independent fair random bits. Its worst-case running time, over all random tapes, is polynomial in the binary input length. It always returns a feasible solution, and its expected cost is measured over its coins. A real number \(r\ge1\) is achievable if one such algorithm satisfies \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{cost}(A(I))]\le r\operatorname{OPT}(I)\) for every valid instance I. The target is the infimum of achievable r; the polynomial and algorithm may depend on r. An infimum need not be attained. All integers and rational input data use explicit binary encodings, with numerator and positive denominator for each rational; their full lengths count toward the input size. No complexity assumption is built into the definition.

context_blocks.text: The problem minimizes squared distances with a strict center budget. Fixed-dimensional schemes and algorithms whose time is exponential in k do not determine the unrestricted polynomial-time ratio.
The STOC 2026 bound is followed by a July preprint reporting a ratio approaching 3 + ln 2. The introduction explicitly treats unrestricted Euclidean centers, which is the model used here.

why: Resolve the fundamental computational approximation limit of a central clustering objective, beyond successive improvements to particular algorithms.

progress.text: The STOC paper gives ratios approaching four for Euclidean k-means.
The spectral dual-fitting preprint reports ratios approaching 3 + ln 2. It does not establish a matching unrestricted computational lower bound.

answer_criterion: Supply a real number a and a complete Lean-checked proof that its absolute difference from the defined constant is at most \(1/100\). A proved containing interval of width at most \(1/50\) qualifies through its midpoint. The constant is unconditional: a lower bound relying on an unproved complexity assumption settles only the corresponding conditional statement. Merely restating the defining infimum is not a determination.

sentences: Euclidean k-means chooses k arbitrary centers to minimize the sum of squared distances.
The dimension and cluster count are both part of the input.
The target is the best ratio achievable by any uniform randomized polynomial-time algorithm.
Recent 2026 algorithms improve the upper bound without determining that infimum.
A certified value within 0.01 requires control of both the achievable ratios and the lower bound.
